evals.name: synthesise-5-interview-transcripts
evals.prompt:
Synthesise 5 interviews I ran with B2B admins (5-50 seat accounts) about team management. I'll describe each interview briefly since you don't have the transcripts — treat this as realistic input and produce a full thematic synthesis following standard coding practice.

P01 (Ops Lead, 12-person team): 'I spend 45 minutes every week reconciling who has access to what. Our spreadsheet is out of date within a day.' Mentions SSO 3 times. Frustrated about role changes not propagating. Would pay for bulk permission audits.
P02 (CTO, 8-person team): 'Honestly, I delegate this to an intern. I don't care about the tool as long as people get in.' Low engagement signal. Uses basic admin console monthly.
P03 (Head of People, 30-person team): Long discussion about compliance — SOC 2 audit next quarter. Needs exportable audit logs. Mentions that 'any change should leave a trail'. Strong pain on off-boarding.
P04 (Team Lead, 18-person team): 'I just want to add Sarah to the project — why do I need to go through the admin page?' Delegation story. Self-serve permissions at a lower level is the wish.
P05 (Founder, 7-person team): 'We're too small for this to matter. I do it in 5 minutes.' Explicitly says this isn't a priority at their size.

Produce the synthesis: ranked themes with evidence strength + segment pattern + representative quotes + implications + triangulation-with-quant suggestions.
evals.expected_output: A ranked-themes synthesis: each theme with frequency (N/5 sources), segment pattern, 2-3 quotes with participant IDs, implication (what product should investigate/change), counter-evidence called out, confidence level, and next quant check suggested. Evidence bar: 3+ sources = real theme.

evals.name: triangulate-checkout-confusion
evals.prompt: Triangulate this claim and recommend action. Claim: 'our checkout is confusing to users and this is costing us conversions'. Qualitative evidence: 7 of 12 interviewed B2B admins (in the last 30 days) mention 'confusing' or 'overwhelming' unprompted when describing the checkout flow. Quantitative evidence: funnel drop-off from checkout_started to checkout_completed is 42% (benchmark in our industry is 15-20%). Segment cut: drop-off concentrated in 3+ seat purchases (56% drop) vs 1-2 seat (29% drop). Segment in the interview sample: all were 5-50 seat. Guardrails: support tickets tagged 'billing/checkout' up 18% last quarter. Triangulate, state confidence, name what would change the conclusion, recommend action.
evals.expected_output: A triangulation memo: claim restated, quali evidence assessed (strength + counter-evidence), quant evidence assessed (magnitude, segment pattern, baseline comparison), comparison table, combined confidence (high/med/low) with rationale, implication for product, what would flip the conclusion, recommended next action (specific).
